LLM_description:
1. Situation:
Multiple forward units across the brigade area require sustained resupply of ammunition, fuel, and rations from rear-area depots over the coming operational period. Terrain includes a mountainous valley dominated by enemy observation, with choke points vulnerable to indirect fire and IEDs. Main supply routes are intermittently interdicted; alternate routes are longer and less developed. Weather and darkness reduce convoy speed and constrain movement windows. The available ground transport fleet is limited, and escort assets are not sufficient to cover all routes simultaneously.

2. Mission:
Deliver required supplies from depots to designated units while minimizing total operational cost, encompassing transport costs, shortage penalty costs, vehicle deployment costs, and fixed route security risk costs. Maintain unit combat effectiveness and readiness by meeting critical demands under the stated constraints.

3. Execution/Concept:
- Distribution Approach: Centrally coordinate shipments from Supply Depot Bravo, Depot Sierra, and other rear nodes to forward locations including FOB Alpha, COP Hammer, Fire Base Orion, and Outpost Kestrel. Plan daily convoy movements by supply type and destination, allocating vehicles and selecting routes that balance risk, cost, and urgency.
- Constraints:
  • Depot Capacity: Outbound shipments from each depot by supply type cannot exceed on-hand, releasable stocks for the period.
  • Demand Fulfillment: Each unit’s daily requirement by supply type must be met by aggregated deliveries across depots. Controlled shortfalls are permissible when necessary; any unmet demand will be recorded and penalized.
  • Vehicle Capacity: Convoy loads must respect vehicle payload limits, computed using each supply’s volume factor. Loads exceeding capacity are not authorized.
  • Route Activation: Vehicles may only be dispatched on routes designated as active for that day. Activating a route—sending any number of vehicles—incurs a fixed Risk Cost representing escort teams, route clearance, overwatch, and ISR, regardless of the number of vehicles employed.
  • Fleet Size: Total vehicles assigned across all routes in a day cannot exceed the fleet available.
- Risk Considerations: Enemy interdiction along the valley MSR necessitates route clearance and armed escort. Alternate routes through the ridge line avoid direct fires but increase travel time and exposure to mechanical failure. Weather degradation and limited visibility require daytime movement for bulk convoys; night moves reserved for high-priority, low-signature loads.
- Priorities: Immediate resupply of maneuver battalions’ ammunition and fuel takes precedence. Rations and noncritical classes are deferred if necessary, with associated penalty costs accepted. Backhaul opportunities will be used to reposition empty vehicles and redistribute depot stocks efficiently.
- Coordination: Movement control will issue convoy manifests and route activation orders. Engineers and EOD synchronize clearance. Fires and ISR provide overwatch for activated routes. Logistics status is updated daily to re-optimize flows, vehicle assignments, and route selections.

LLM_description_template:
1. Situation:
- The Corps is sustaining dispersed maneuver elements in contested terrain. Ground lines of communication are intermittently interdicted by enemy activity and affected by weather and damaged infrastructure.
- Multiple rear-area supply depots hold stocks by class and by day. Forward units at several forward operating bases have daily, time-phased demands that cannot be fully pre-positioned due to mobility and protection constraints.
- Movement corridors vary in distance, terrain, and security posture. Some routes require engineering clearance, EOD sweeps, and armed escort. Activating any such route on a given day (i.e., sending any vehicles at all) incurs a fixed security Risk Cost for that route-day, regardless of the number of vehicles dispatched. Per-vehicle deployment costs and transport costs are accounted for separately.
- The ground fleet is limited and centrally controlled. Vehicles have fixed capacity; mixed loads are constrained by supply volumes. Convoys may be split across depots and units as needed.

2. Mission:
- Deliver required supplies to supported units across the planning horizon while minimizing total operational cost, comprising: transport costs by depot-to-unit route, penalties for unmet daily demand, per-vehicle deployment costs, and fixed route security Risk Costs for each activated route-day.

3. Execution/Concept:
- Allocate daily flows by supply class from depots to units, respecting depot stock limits by day. Split shipments across multiple depots and routes where advantageous.
- Size convoys based on supply volumes and vehicle capacity. Vehicles may only move on routes activated for the day. If a route is activated, the fixed Risk Cost applies even if only one vehicle uses it that day.
- Enforce a daily cap on total vehicles dispatched across all routes to reflect fleet availability. Prioritize lower-cost, lower-risk corridors; activate higher-risk routes only when the expected benefit outweighs the fixed security overhead.
- Meet unit demands to the maximum extent; where operationally justified, accept controlled shortfalls, incurring penalty costs that represent operational risk and degraded readiness.
- Coordinating Instructions:
  - Engineers and EOD conduct route clearance on activated corridors; Military Police provide escort teams as required.
  - Movement Control allocates vehicles and deconflicts convoy timing.
  - Daily route activation decisions are made at the logistics operations center based on updated threat and weather. Adjust flows dynamically as conditions change.
